method.method_draft: Read the diagram as rectangle EFGH with E at the upper left, F upper right, G lower right, H lower left, and diagonal EG drawn from E to G. From the text, use that EFGH is a rectangle and that m∠FEG = 57°. In a rectangle, the corner angle ∠FEH at E is 90°. The diagonal EG lies inside that right angle and splits it into adjacent angles ∠FEG and ∠GEH. Therefore m∠GEH = 90° - 57° = 33°.

method.method_draft: Read the image as rectangle EFGH with diagonal EG, and note the marked right angle at H between EH and HG. From the text, m∠FEG = 57°. Since EFGH is a rectangle, EF is parallel to HG. With EG as a transversal, ∠FEG equals ∠EGH, so m∠EGH = 57°. Now consider triangle EHG: ∠EHG = 90° and ∠EGH = 57°. By the triangle angle sum, m∠GEH = 180° - 90° - 57° = 33°.
